data.text:
The tdd gate refused a citation of checks 54, 55, 58 and 59, and it was right to,
but the reason is a limit of SEEN-113's content test that SEEN-113 could not have
seen on itself. It is recorded here because SEEN-008 is the first ticket other than
SEEN-113 to exercise that rule.

The rule tests content rather than attempt number: a check taken in an earlier attempt
still supports a citation when no file the slice covers has moved since it ran. To
scope that comparison it must first find which commit on the branch carries the tree
the check ran against, by recomputing each commit's content fingerprint. When it finds
no such commit it cannot tell which files moved, so it falls back to comparing the whole
tree and refuses.

A rebase destroys that anchor by construction. Replaying the branch onto a moved main
gives every commit a new tree, so no commit's fingerprint can match one taken before
the rebase, whatever the slice's own files did. Here the branch was rebased onto the
main that carries SEEN-113 itself, and the measurement is exact: `git diff --name-only
116c801 HEAD -- supabase/migrations packages/core/db turbo.json docs/architecture.md`
is empty. Every file either cited slice covers is byte-identical across the rebase.
What moved was 96 records of SEEN-113's own journal, its harness code, its ticket,
graphify-out and CLAUDE.md, and none of it is content either check was about.

So the evidence is intact in substance and unciteable in form. The refusal is still the
correct behaviour: once the anchor is gone the rule cannot distinguish a slice whose files
are identical from one whose files changed, and a rule that guessed between those would be
worth less than one that refuses. The defect is that the anchor is a whole-tree fingerprint
when the question is about a named set of files, and a rebase is an ordinary act that the
delivery procedure itself requires before a pull request can merge.

The checks are therefore being re-run in this attempt rather than argued into citability.
This is the fourth defect SEEN-112's proof run and its successors have surfaced in the
harness rather than in the ticket under work, after the guard that stops guarding during
rework, the guard that cannot express a directory, and the coverage command whose `--`
pnpm forwards. All four want one harness ticket.
